title: PPWR and EPR: Could the Local Representative Requirement Be Suspended?
metaTitle: PPWR and EPR: Could the Local Representative Requirement Be Suspended?
description: Could the EU suspend the packaging EPR representative requirement? Compare the Commission, Parliament and Council proposals and see what still applies.
imageAlt: Vareya illustration about the proposed PPWR and EPR representative suspension
caption: 2035 was the European Commission’s proposed date, not an agreed deadline.

content: The EU has not adopted the proposed suspension. The Commission originally proposed 1 January 2035, but Parliament and the Council have different negotiating positions. The current requirements still apply.

The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) has generally applied since 12 August 2026. Article 45(3) requires certain EU-established producers selling packaging or packaged products directly to end users in another Member State to appoint a representative there for extended producer responsibility (EPR) by written mandate. Member States may also require a representative for third-country producers.

The proposed change concerns the appointment requirement for certain EU-established producers. It would not postpone the PPWR as a whole or remove other duties such as registration, reporting and financial contributions where these apply.
The Short Answer: Is the PPWR Being Delayed Until 2035?

No. The proposal does not postpone the entire PPWR. It concerns the mandatory appointment of an authorised representative for extended producer responsibility. Other EPR obligations would continue to apply.
The distinction matters:

rows: Possible temporary suspension for some EU-established producers

content: The proposed relief therefore concerns how businesses organise their obligations, rather than removing their responsibility for packaging waste.
What Are PPWR and EPR?

The PPWR, Regulation (EU) 2025/40, governs which packaging can be placed on the European market and includes measures addressing packaging waste and waste prevention. Its implementation involves different requirements and application dates; not every provision takes effect at the same time.

EPR stands for Extended Producer Responsibility. The principle is that the responsible producer contributes to the costs of managing the waste generated by the packaging it places on the market. Depending on the applicable rules, this can involve registration, reporting and financial contributions.

For international online retailers, an important consideration is that practical EPR arrangements still differ between countries. Selling within a single European market does not automatically mean one registration or one declaration covers every destination country.
What Does an Authorised Representative Do?

An EPR representative acts on behalf of a producer in fulfilling obligations in a country where that producer is not established. The purpose is to support compliance and enforcement, including when the seller operates from another country.

The current PPWR framework includes a representative requirement for certain producers supplying packaging or packaged products directly to end users in another EU Member State. The specific assessment depends on the legal entity and its role in the sales chain.
An international compliance provider may coordinate the service. However, that coordination should be distinguished from the local representation required under the applicable rules.
What Is the European Commission Proposing?
On 10 December 2025, the European Commission published proposal COM(2025) 982 final, part of the Environmental Omnibus package. The legislative procedure number is 2025/0395(COD).

Article 2 of the proposal specifically addresses the suspension of Article 45(3) of the PPWR until 1 January 2035. The Commission’s objective is to reduce administrative burdens for producers established in the EU that sell in other Member States. Under the original proposal, appointing a representative would become voluntary for those producers during the suspension period.
This is therefore not a requirement that would only begin in 2035. It is a proposed temporary suspension of an existing requirement.
Why Is the Outcome Still Uncertain?
The European institutions have different negotiating positions. None of these positions changes the law by itself.

rows: Original proposal: eligible EU-established producers selling across Member States.
The amendments adopted on 20 October would limit the relief to EU-based micro and small enterprises.
Until 1 January 2035, or earlier if horizontal EU EPR legislation applies.
Its 21 October negotiating position would cover EU-established packaging producers placing less than one tonne per destination Member State and calendar year.
Until 1 January 2032, with a review by the end of 2030.

content: The Commission’s presentation registered on 5 November said negotiations were ongoing and encouraged pragmatic enforcement. That is not an exemption. Continue to check the rules for the applicable producer, packaging flow and destination.
What Does This Mean for Ecommerce Businesses Shipping from the Netherlands?
A Dutch fulfilment warehouse can centralise physical order processing. It does not automatically centralise packaging compliance obligations in every destination country.
A proper assessment should address questions such as:

items: Which legal entity sells to the end customer?
In which countries are products sold?
Which EPR registrations and contracts are already in place?
Who supplies the product packaging, and who adds the shipping packaging?

content: Use this information to have a specialist assess the applicable obligations in each country. Distinguish between registration, reporting, financial contributions and representation. These are related but separate responsibilities.
What Can Businesses Prepare Now?
Even if the representative requirement is suspended, reliable packaging records will remain valuable. The proposal does not remove other EPR obligations.
A practical preparation process has three steps.
1. Review Existing Coverage
Collect registration numbers, contracts, declarations and payment records. Record which legal entity, countries and packaging streams each arrangement covers.
2. Make Packaging Data Verifiable
Document the material, weight, dimensions and available supplier information for each packaging component. Keep product packaging and added shipping packaging separately identifiable.
3. Define Responsibilities in Writing

Agree who collects the data, who checks it and who handles registrations, declarations and payments. Do not assume that a fulfilment partner also acts as an EPR representative unless this has been explicitly agreed in writing.
What Role Can a Fulfilment Partner Play?
A fulfilment partner’s most natural contribution is operational: providing visibility into shipping packaging, order profiles, destination countries and the execution of packaging instructions.

For Vareya, the proposed approach is to connect that operational information with the requirements established by the customer and its compliance adviser. The availability of specific data, reports or additional support must be agreed in advance. Specialist registrations and formal representation require separately confirmed services.

Packaging optimisation also deserves attention. A smaller or lighter packaging format may offer benefits, but it should always be assessed against product protection, operational practicality and substantiated material properties. Choosing paper or cardboard alone does not demonstrate compliance with every applicable requirement.
Conclusion: Prepare, but Keep the Distinctions Clear

A temporary suspension could matter to ecommerce businesses selling in several EU countries, but the scope and date are not agreed. It could simplify the administrative organisation of EPR. However, the proposal does not mean that the PPWR or all packaging obligations would be postponed until 2035.
The most sensible approach is twofold: follow the legislative process while making sure legal entities, existing registrations, packaging data and responsibilities are clearly documented.
